question: Do modified Kneser–Ney, masked recurrent/transformer models, metadata and outside-population text improve the saved Paper 001 known-slot benchmark, and do learning curves show remaining data gains?
outcome: MKN without extra: 39.7178% top-one, 4.581891 bits on 8,009 identical queries. Neural families alone do not beat MKN; ensemble with extra: 41.1662%, 4.347675 native bits. Extra text gives no measurable top-one gain; 72–94% of its common-loss gain comes from 251 outside-alphabet targets (94% for MKN, −0.2990 bits total). All four curves rise 1.21–1.71 points from 75% to 100% training.
challenge: Paper 001 component-held-out independence: 16 identical one-/two-sign texts on different objects create 144–159 linked training strings/fold, joining 192 strings and 748 queries (9.3%); no links with a three-sign threshold. Reviewer removal estimates: −8.02/−8.96/−5.88 touched-query points for first/second/MKN, implied −0.75/−0.84/−0.55 benchmark points; ranking unchanged, paired shifts at most 0.30 points. One-edit neighbours cover 509 strings (31.9%), with removal estimates −1.47/−2.32/−1.80 benchmark points. Reused masks, outcome-defined frequency ECE, post-outcome auxiliary loss and transformer epoch cap constrain interpretation.
remedy: Exact query correspondence, nested selection and full extra-face closure verified by the reviewer. Preserve numerical endpoints and frozen recipe; append dated smoothing/timing/epoch errata; use reviewer graph, neighbour and loss-decomposition evidence, position calibration and refreshed plotting metadata.
retry_when: A newly acquired source-reviewed population can test the frozen recipe without retuning; any longer-training or different neural family needs a new exploratory protocol and fresh endpoints.
